section_summary: This section documents U.S. State Department and SCAP policies and reporting from October 1946 to February 1949 regarding minority populations in occupied Japan, primarily focusing on the status, treatment, and unrest of Korean residents following World War II. It details violent Korean protests in Kobe and Osaka over Japanese school closures, the resulting military intervention and mass arrests, and reactions from Korean communities in Shanghai and the military government in Seoul. Extensive GHQ SCAP staff studies and diplomatic correspondence analyze options for voluntary Korean repatriation, property transfer regulations, nationality determinations, and the rejection of special foreign national privileges for Korean residents.

subfiles.about: Discusses the nationality and treatment of Formosans in Japan and submits a proposed draft cable to SCAP.
subfiles.summary: Memorandum recommending approval of a draft cable to SCAP regarding the nationality and treatment of Formosans in Japan.
subfiles.title: Nationality and Treatment of Formosans

subfiles.about: Reports on the reactions of the Shanghai Korean community to school closures and Korean arrests in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Reports Shanghai Koreans' protests against Japanese police actions and school closures, community attitudes toward South Korean elections, and internal factional politics.
subfiles.title: Reaction of Shanghai-Korean Community to Closure of Korean Schools and Arrests of Koreans in Japan; Information concerning Korean Community

subfiles.about: Translation of a draft protest letter from Shanghai Koreans to the Japanese government regarding Korean schools and arrests.
subfiles.from: Association for Upholding the Rights of Koreans in Japan
subfiles.summary: Protest demanding the reopening of Korean schools in Japan, release of arrested Koreans, compensation, and foreign national status.
subfiles.title: Korean Residents Here Draft Letter of Protest to Japanese Government

subfiles.about: Transmits a letter from the American Consul at Kobe describing Korean demonstrations in Kobe.
subfiles.summary: Cover despatch transmitting a report from the American Consul at Kobe concerning recent Korean demonstrations and police response.
subfiles.title: Korean Demonstrations in Kobe, Japan

subfiles.about: Detailed report on Korean demonstrations in Kobe protesting school closures, mobbing of the prefectural office, and Eighth Army intervention.
subfiles.summary: Describes April 1948 Korean protests in Kobe over school closures, coercion of the prefectural governor, subsequent Eighth Army intervention, mass arrests, and local military handling.
subfiles.title: Notes on Recent Korean Demonstrations in Kobe

subfiles.about: Form designating an attached copy of Despatch 270 as the official record copy to replace the unreturned original.
subfiles.summary: Form designating the attached copy of Tokyo Despatch 270 as the official record copy replacing the missing original.
subfiles.title: Record Copy Replacement Form for Despatch No. 270

subfiles.about: True copy of Despatch No. 270 transmitting a letter on Korean demonstrations in Kobe.
subfiles.summary: Certified duplicate record copy of Despatch 270 transmitting the Kobe Consul's report on Korean demonstrations.
subfiles.title: Korean Demonstrations in Kobe, Japan

subfiles.about: Internal memorandum commenting on Seoul Despatch No. 122 and General Dean's statement on Korean riots in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Transmits and briefly evaluates General Dean's press statement concerning Korean school riots in Japan.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 122

subfiles.about: Transmits Major General William F. Dean's press release on Korean riots in Japan caused by school closures.
subfiles.summary: Cover despatch transmitting Major General William F. Dean's press statement concerning Korean school riots in Japan.
subfiles.title: Military Governor's Statement on Korean Riots in Japan

subfiles.about: Press release addressing Korean school riots in Japan, educational rights under Japanese law, and political agitation.
subfiles.summary: General Dean condemns communist exploitation of school disputes in Japan, explains that Korean residents must obey Japanese educational laws, and highlights accreditation procedures.
subfiles.title: General Dean's Answer to Written Press Questions of May 6, 1948

subfiles.about: Reports on an Ainu chieftain's appeal to General Shang Chen for Chiang Kai-shek's help in securing an Ainu tribal reservation.
subfiles.summary: Reports an appeal by an Ainu chieftain from Hokkaido to Chinese Mission head General Shang Chen seeking Chinese support for an Ainu reservation.
subfiles.title: Ainus in Hokkaido

subfiles.about: Transmits GHQ SCAP Diplomatic Section staff study and check sheets regarding policies for the treatment and status of Koreans in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Transmits SCAP Diplomatic Section staff study on the status of Koreans in Japan, noting commendation by MacArthur and implementation of currency relaxation.
subfiles.title: Status of Koreans in Japan

subfiles.about: Comprehensive staff study analyzing the legal, economic, and political problems of Koreans in Japan and recommending policy measures.
subfiles.summary: This comprehensive staff study analyzes the legal, political, and economic problems posed by roughly 600,000 Koreans residing in Japan following the establishment of the South Korean government. It recommends reopening voluntary mass repatriation with significantly relaxed currency and property limits, while deferring final determination of nationality for those remaining to a future bilateral treaty between Japan and Korea. It further advises treating Koreans who remain as Japanese nationals without special foreign or UN national privileges, and accrediting a Korean diplomatic representative to SCAP if requested.
subfiles.title: Staff Study Concerning Koreans in Japan

subfiles.about: Submits draft staff study on Koreans in Japan to Chief of Staff for approval and outlines recommended implementation steps.
subfiles.summary: Forwards draft staff study on Koreans in Japan for approval, summarizes key recommendations, and outlines operational implementation steps across staff sections.
subfiles.title: Check Sheet: Staff Study Recommending Policies for Treatment of Koreans in Japan

subfiles.about: Returns staff study approving relaxation of currency restrictions and noting General MacArthur's commendation.
subfiles.summary: Approves relaxing currency and property transfer restrictions for repatriates, holds broader recommendations as future guidance, and conveys MacArthur's commendation.
subfiles.title: Check Sheet: Status of Koreans in Japan

subfiles.about: Transmits copy of Tokyo Despatch 580 and the SCAP staff study concerning Koreans in Japan to the Department of the Army.
subfiles.summary: Transmits a copy of Tokyo Despatch 580 and the SCAP staff study on Koreans in Japan to General Eberle for consideration.
subfiles.title: Letter to General Eberle Regarding Staff Study on Koreans in Japan

subfiles.about: Analyzes and endorses Richard B. Finn's staff study on Korean repatriation and nationality in Tokyo Despatch 580.
subfiles.summary: Reviews and strongly endorses Richard B. Finn's recommendations in Tokyo Despatch 580 regarding voluntary Korean repatriation, nationality deferral, and avoiding special privileges.
subfiles.title: Attached: Tokyo's 580

subfiles.about: Inquires about a constituent's letter alleging racial segregation between Allied personnel and Japanese in Tokyo.
subfiles.summary: Quotes a constituent's letter reporting a foreign student's claims of racial segregation between Allied personnel and Japanese in Tokyo, requesting an official explanation.
subfiles.title: Inquiry Regarding Allegations of Racial Segregation in Occupied Japan

subfiles.about: Refutes allegations of racial street segregation in Japan, clarifying that separate facilities are for Occupation operational efficiency.
subfiles.summary: Denies racial street segregation in occupied Japan, explaining that separate facilities and transport designations for Allied personnel are standard operational procedures.
subfiles.title: Reply to Representative Judd Regarding Facilities in Occupied Japan

subfiles.about: Reports ongoing policy discussions on reducing the Korean minority in Japan and transmits a memorandum on nationality and registration.
subfiles.summary: Discusses reducing Japan's Korean minority, withholding general recognition of Korean nationality for residents, and transmits a preparatory study and Japanese Foreign Office conversation memorandum.
subfiles.title: Status of Koreans in Japan

subfiles.about: Detailed memorandum analyzing nationality registration, property transfer, and food rations for Koreans in Japan.
subfiles.from: Office of the United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.summary: Analyzes policies toward Koreans in Japan, arguing against general registration as Korean nationals by the Korean Liaison Mission. Recommends encouraging voluntary repatriation through relaxed property rules while maintaining treatment as Japanese nationals to avoid onerous extra food ration burdens and dual nationality complications.
subfiles.title: Memorandum: Status of Koreans in Japan
